```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day bar is a single paying customer. B is a one-sided subscription, so one podcaster paying about $19/mo meets it. A gets paid mainly through closing fees, which need a buyer, a seller and a completed deal, all inside 90 days.",
    "A's own brief names buyer-side liquidity as the documented failure mode. The closest comparable has 500+ visitors a day and 30 listings, yet reports that buyers are slow to convert two weeks in. B has no equivalent cold-start problem.",
    "A's one paid-acquisition data point is negative: a $750 newsletter sponsorship to a similar audience produced 124 clicks and zero sales. B's channel evidence is sourced cost data (Google CPC $2-3, Meta CPC $0.26-0.50, $100-500/mo budgets) with no recorded failure.",
    "B's demand evidence is three sourced Reddit quotes from paying-segment users who say hosting costs too much. That points directly at a 'cheaper or simpler host' wedge. A's demand quotes are all from sellers, and one comes from a competitor reporting weak buyer conversion.",
    "Both markets are crowded with free or 0%-commission incumbents. B's setup is simpler: Stripe billing and a privacy-policy review. A needs licensed escrow, a state-by-state broker-licensing check, and handling of sensitive financial data that the brief itself flags as unsourced.",
    "B's main risk is ops cost: storage, CDN and RSS uptime. That hurts margin and scale, but it does not stop a first sale the way A's two-sided liquidity problem does."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's central 'Case For' is the claim that AI agents can replicate Acquire.com's human acquisition-expert services at near-zero marginal cost and out-service incumbents in sub-$10k deals. No source shows that this works or that buyers would value it. Behind it, the buyer side has no demand evidence at all: no quote, no data point and no channel result shows buyers will come to and transact on a new solo-run marketplace. The only buyer-side signals are negative (slow buyer conversion at DealMyApp, zero sales from the $750 sponsorship).",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Both briefs describe saturated categories, and neither shows evidence of a sharp, defensible wedge. B also has gaps: it cites seven competitors but lists five, the 'race to the bottom' Reddit comment is unlinked, the cost of organic community acquisition is unsourced, and gross margin after hosting costs is unknown. The pick rests mostly on structure: a one-sided subscription is far easier to get a first payment from within 90 days than a two-sided marketplace that earns on close. It does not rest on B's evidence being strong in absolute terms."
}
```
